# Issue 223 dependency refresh

The starting point is main commit `5c2804cf476e3eb4aed7ac09e2245e2617b447ab`. Dependabot PRs #212 and #222 were already merged. Issue 223 had one follow-up with the baseline CI results and no registered sub-issues. PR 224 initially contained only a draft placeholder and had no conversation comments, review comments or reviews.

[Issue and follow-up](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/issues/223) · [Pull request](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/pull/224) · [Previous dependency refresh](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/pull/103)

## Requirements and plan

| Requirement | Options and implementation plan | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Repair errors caused by the already-merged Dependabot updates | Compare failed and succeeding runs on main to isolate persistent regressions. Reproduce the formatter failure with the version in the baseline lock, then apply its output. Keep the merged upgrades. | Baseline log lines, formatter before and after, audit results and the PR check suite. |
| Update every JavaScript and TypeScript dependency, including dev tools and transitives | Compare the registry latest dist-tag with all active manifests, overrides, npm lock entries and Deno lock entries. Use the native npm resolver after adjusting direct constraints. Resolve Deno's graph separately with its own tool. Review consumer ranges before imposing a transitive major. | Three clean npm installs, frozen Deno graph, lock inventories, lint, Node/Bun/Deno tests and the example build. |
| Update Python, the benchmark model and every Python tool | Compare with PyPI and model releases. Resolve the benchmark graph with uv and regenerate hashes for the tested Python version. Refresh the Python 3.14 requirements file specifically named in the issue. Its original version remains available at the baseline commit. | Ruff, hash-locked scanner smoke and pip-audit on both active and captured requirements. |
| Update all external workflow and composite references, toolchains, images and inline tools | Resolve Action releases and the commit behind each SHA pin, preserve pinning style, and keep versions synchronized where repeated. Compare image manifests with registry digests. | Actionlint, zizmor, ShellCheck, native build jobs and cross-runtime release checks. |
| Keep Dependabot coverage complete | Keep grouped npm, pip and GitHub Actions updates. Add coverage for any missing active manifest or for a named historical directory if the issue explicitly requires it. | Compare directory coverage with the actual manifests and the GitHub documentation. |
| Review major migrations and use upstream functionality | Review primary release notes and actual call sites. Remove a workaround when an upstream release supplies equivalent behavior, and verify callers through the existing entry point. | Migration notes with links and focused regression checks. |
| Report remaining reusable logic, gaps and defects upstream | Review prior reports from PR 103 and search for duplicates before creating or updating a report. Include a reproducer, versions, workaround and proposed change for confirmed cases. | Upstream report URLs and affected integration notes in PR 224. |
| Record every old, latest and selected version, with a reason for each exception | Query the registries before editing and reconcile the resulting npm, Deno, PyPI, Action and toolchain inventories against the final graph. | Dependency tables and compatibility evidence in this folder. |
| Ship one tested PR with a normal release trigger | Add a major changeset for the Node engine floor, merge any new main commits into the prepared branch, update PR 224 with a closing keyword and verify checks against the final head SHA. | Clean working tree, actual PR diff, CI results and the release guard. |

## Existing components

- npm's native resolver and registry audit work against a committed lockfile. npm-check-updates can discover new direct majors. Registry dist-tags still need to be compared with the locks for transitive packages. [npm audit and lockfile behavior](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/audit/) · [npm-check-updates](https://github.com/raineorshine/npm-check-updates)
- Deno's supported reproducible workflow is `deno ci`. `deno install --frozen=false` updates the graph before CI verifies it. [Deno dependency management](https://docs.deno.com/runtime/packages/)
- uv compiles a complete, hash-pinned requirements file without installing the NLP stack to discover versions. pip-audit can audit that resolved graph. [uv requirements compilation](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/pip/compile/) · [pip-audit](https://github.com/pypa/pip-audit)
- Dependabot already manages grouped updates in this repository. Renovate also supports package managers and inline dependency extraction when an upstream ecosystem has no native manifest. [Dependabot options](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/working-with-dependabot/dependabot-options-reference) · [Renovate custom managers](https://docs.renovatebot.com/modules/manager/regex/)

## Version inventories

Registry metadata was collected on 2026-11-20 UTC. Baseline rows use the original merge base. Blank selections identify lock locations or packages removed by the new resolution. A newer registry version may be outside a consumer's supported range. The tables identify that consumer and, where npm records it, its declared range. The npm registry's `latest` dist-tag for the NLP.js family points to an alpha even though a stable 4.x line is available.

- [Root npm lock](npm-root.csv), [example app npm lock](npm-app.csv) and [artifact transport npm lock](npm-artifact.csv) include added, retained, hoisted and removed entries. The local temp-rimraf shim has no external dependencies. It remains in the example lock.
- [Deno lock](deno.csv) includes peer-dependent npm locations and the consumers resolving each held version.
- [Python](python.csv) covers the active requirements, hash lock, the Python 3.14 requirements file named by the issue, and isolated CI tooling. Dependabot now names both Python directories. Its pip fetcher looks at requirements content in `.txt` files, including this filename. [Dependabot pip file discovery](https://github.com/dependabot/dependabot-core/blob/main/python/lib/dependabot/python/shared_file_fetcher.rb) · [Original Python evidence at the baseline commit](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/5c2804cf476e3eb4aed7ac09e2245e2617b447ab/dev/log/issues/102/pulls/103/research/requirements-python314.txt)
- [GitHub Actions](github-actions.csv) lists each external action, hosted action digest and in-repository composite occurrence. The CodeQL bundle and the GitHub Action have independent release tags.
- [Toolchains, images and binaries](toolchains.csv) covers external releases outside the dependency locks. Shell scripts and HTML use tools and asset packages from these existing ecosystems. The repository has no active Dockerfile, Cargo, Go, Gradle, Xcode or other native package manifest. Capacitor generates the Android and iOS projects from the app's npm pins.

## Migration decisions

- `command-stream` 3 removes terminal and recording dependencies from its default installation. The sanitizer uses the shell tag and `command-stream/execa`. It does not call the moved PTY or recording APIs. Browser Commander still declares the 2.x range, so development installs retain a separate 2.x graph. [Command Stream 3 release](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/releases/tag/js-v3.0.0) · [Browser Commander report](https://github.com/link-foundation/browser-commander/issues/193)
- `lino-objects-codec` 1.0.0 keeps the existing codec integration and requires Node 26.13.1 and npm 12.2.2 or later. The project now uses Node 26.13.1 and npm 12.2.3 and has a major changeset for the Node support change. Node, Bun and Deno support the native `RegExp.escape` used by the NER vocabulary builder and changeset package matcher in place of two local implementations. Lino i18n still declares a separate 0.9 codec range. [Codec 1 release](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-objects-codec/releases/tag/js_v1.0.0) · [Lino i18n report](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n/issues/45)
- CPython stays on its latest 3.14 patch because current Presidio publishes `Requires-Python: >=3.11,<3.15`, plus caps on NumPy and preshed. Prior CI reached a native failure in `spacy.load("en_core_web_sm")` from the constrained 3.15 graph. Use a hash-locked install and load the actual model when retesting. [Presidio metadata](https://pypi.org/pypi/presidio-analyzer/2.2.366/json) · [Upstream reproduction](https://github.com/data-privacy-stack/presidio/issues/2431#issuecomment-6673100519)
- Java uses current Temurin 21 with a matching Gradle runtime. The generated project uses Gradle 8.14.3, Android Gradle Plugin 8.13.0 and Android SDK API 36. A Java 27 migration would require a Gradle 9 migration outside the current Capacitor template. Setup Java 6.3 makes annotations opt-in, so the workflow explicitly keeps the problem matcher. [Latest Temurin 21](https://github.com/adoptium/temurin21-binaries/releases/latest) · [Gradle Java matrix](https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/compatibility.html#java_runtime) · [Capacitor 8 migration](https://capacitorjs.com/docs/updating/8-0) · [Setup Java 6.3 release](https://github.com/actions/setup-java/releases/tag/v6.3.0)
- Upstream consumers own the transitive terminal-formatting major transitions. The reviewed pure-ESM and output changes cover ANSI detection/styling, emoji patterns, string width, and sisteransi. There are no direct imports of these transitive libraries from shipped or CI code. Both npm example packaging and the runtime suite exercise the parent tools. [ansi-regex](https://github.com/chalk/ansi-regex/releases) · [ansi-styles](https://github.com/chalk/ansi-styles/releases) · [emoji-regex](https://github.com/mathiasbynens/emoji-regex/releases) · [string-width](https://github.com/sindresorhus/string-width/releases) · [strip-ansi](https://github.com/chalk/strip-ansi/releases) · [sisteransi](https://www.npmjs.com/package/sisteransi)
- Both Playwright images use the registry digest for the locked Playwright 1.65.1 release. The workflow regression test checks the tag and digest in both jobs against the npm version. BuildKit’s canonical and fallback registry tags resolve to the same manifest digest. Betterleaks 1.10.1 ships the same configuration checksum and 203-rule catalog as the prior patch. [Playwright release notes](https://playwright.dev/docs/release-notes) · [Buildx release](https://github.com/docker/buildx/releases/tag/v0.39.1) · [Betterleaks release](https://github.com/betterleaks/betterleaks/releases/tag/v1.10.1)

## Upstream reports and retained workarounds

| Report | Reproduction and downstream decision |
| --- | --- |
| [Browser Commander #193](https://github.com/link-foundation/browser-commander/issues/193) | `npm ls` shows Command Stream 2.6.0 and Links Notation 0.25.2 under 0.35.0, alongside this project's newer direct dependencies. Keep upstream ranges pending the capture and config migration. |
| [Lino i18n #45](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n/issues/45) | `npm ls` shows the 0.9 and 1.0 codecs installed side by side. Keep the i18n consumer's 0.9 range pending upstream roundtrip tests. |
| [Actions Toolkit #2582](https://github.com/actions/toolkit/issues/2582) | The current SDK expects `archiver.create`; Archiver 8 exports named archive classes and no longer resolves `archiver-utils` or its glob. Keep the targeted glob override until the SDK migrates. |
| [Scrubadub #157](https://github.com/LeapBeyond/scrubadub/issues/157) | Scrubadub 2.0.1 pins TextBlob 0.15.3, whose two invalid escape sequences warn on CPython 3.14. The current TextBlob passed the same offline scanner smoke in an isolated overlay with `-W error::SyntaxWarning`. Keep the upstream-required pin in the real graph. |
| [Existing upstream reports from PR 103](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/main/dev/log/issues/102/pulls/103/upstream/reports.json) | Covers Node setup-cache ordering, Buildx failover, artifact download/ZIP behavior, the local temp cleanup adapter, Pages, Python wheels and workflow lint grammar. The scoped workarounds remain in place. |
| [Lychee #2297](https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee/issues/2297) | Current Lychee retry classification still misses connect/TLS resets. The existing bounded link recheck remains in the workflow. |

## CI regression evidence

| Finding | Evidence | Fix or disposition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Prettier failure after #222 | At baseline SHA `5c2804c`, main run 44753249623 reported formatting failures for `docs/COVERAGE.md` and `docs/case-studies/issue-128/research/open-source-pii.md` (log lines 786–789). `npm exec --prefix /tmp --package prettier@3.10.1 -- prettier --check <both files>` reproduced exit 1. [Failed main check](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/44753249623) | Commit `357434d` applies the exact locked formatter output. The same command and the full Prettier check pass. |
| Lock audit errors reported in #212 | The two job logs both reported high-severity picomatch 4.0.7 advisory GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf on line 216 with no fix. The advisory was withdrawn on 2026-11-18. [Advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf) · [Original security run](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/44210448243) | Baseline main security run 44753249634 and all three refreshed npm audits pass. The earlier audit error no longer reproduces against current registry data. [Main security](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/44753249634) |
| Runtime matrix asserted a stale Bun version | Run 44756454326 reported an exact Bun 1.4.4 expectation at `tests/transient-links.test.js:127` after upgrading Bun to 1.4.5. [Job annotation](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/44756454326/job/136357933397) | Commit `ac28d99` verifies every setup selects a fixed release in the supported major and the regression test passes on Node, Bun and Deno. |

| Ship one tested PR with a normal release trigger | Add a major changeset for the Node engine floor, merge any new main commits into the prepared branch, update PR 224 with a closing keyword and verify checks against the final head SHA. | Clean working tree, actual PR diff, CI results and the release guard. |

## Existing components

- npm's native resolver and registry audit work against a committed lockfile. npm-check-updates can discover new direct majors. Registry dist-tags still need to be compared with the locks for transitive packages. [npm audit and lockfile behavior](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/audit/) · [npm-check-updates](https://github.com/raineorshine/npm-check-updates)
- Deno's supported reproducible workflow is `deno ci`. `deno install --frozen=false` updates the graph before CI verifies it. [Deno dependency management](https://docs.deno.com/runtime/packages/)
- uv compiles a complete, hash-pinned requirements file without installing the NLP stack to discover versions. pip-audit can audit that resolved graph. [uv requirements compilation](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/pip/compile/) · [pip-audit](https://github.com/pypa/pip-audit)
- Dependabot already manages grouped updates in this repository. Renovate also supports package managers and inline dependency extraction when an upstream ecosystem has no native manifest. [Dependabot options](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/working-with-dependabot/dependabot-options-reference) · [Renovate custom managers](https://docs.renovatebot.com/modules/manager/regex/)

## Version inventories

Registry metadata was collected on 2026-11-20 UTC. Baseline rows use the original merge base. Blank selections identify lock locations or packages removed by the new resolution. A newer registry version may be outside a consumer's supported range. The tables identify that consumer and, where npm records it, its declared range. The npm registry's `latest` dist-tag for the NLP.js family points to an alpha even though a stable 4.x line is available.

- [Root npm lock](npm-root.csv), [example app npm lock](npm-app.csv) and [artifact transport npm lock](npm-artifact.csv) include added, retained, hoisted and removed entries. The local temp-rimraf shim has no external dependencies. It remains in the example lock.
- [Deno lock](deno.csv) includes peer-dependent npm locations and the consumers resolving each held version.
- [Python](python.csv) covers the active requirements, hash lock, the Python 3.14 requirements file named by the issue, and isolated CI tooling. Dependabot now names both Python directories. Its pip fetcher looks at requirements content in `.txt` files, including this filename. [Dependabot pip file discovery](https://github.com/dependabot/dependabot-core/blob/main/python/lib/dependabot/python/shared_file_fetcher.rb) · [Original Python evidence at the baseline commit](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/5c2804cf476e3eb4aed7ac09e2245e2617b447ab/dev/log/issues/102/pulls/103/research/requirements-python314.txt)
- [GitHub Actions](github-actions.csv) lists each external action, hosted action digest and in-repository composite occurrence. The CodeQL bundle and the GitHub Action have independent release tags.
- [Toolchains, images and binaries](toolchains.csv) covers external releases outside the dependency locks. Shell scripts and HTML use tools and asset packages from these existing ecosystems. The repository has no active Dockerfile, Cargo, Go, Gradle, Xcode or other native package manifest. Capacitor generates the Android and iOS projects from the app's npm pins.

## Migration decisions

- `command-stream` 3 removes terminal and recording dependencies from its default installation. The sanitizer uses the shell tag and `command-stream/execa`. It does not call the moved PTY or recording APIs. Browser Commander still declares the 2.x range, so development installs retain a separate 2.x graph. [Command Stream 3 release](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/releases/tag/js-v3.0.0) · [Browser Commander report](https://github.com/link-foundation/browser-commander/issues/193)
- `lino-objects-codec` 1.0.0 keeps the existing codec integration and requires Node 26.13.1 and npm 12.2.2 or later. The project now uses Node 26.13.1 and npm 12.2.3 and has a major changeset for the Node support change. Node, Bun and Deno support the native `RegExp.escape` used by the NER vocabulary builder and changeset package matcher in place of two local implementations. Lino i18n still declares a separate 0.9 codec range. [Codec 1 release](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-objects-codec/releases/tag/js_v1.0.0) · [Lino i18n report](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n/issues/45)
- CPython stays on its latest 3.14 patch because current Presidio publishes `Requires-Python: >=3.11,<3.15`, plus caps on NumPy and preshed. Prior CI reached a native failure in `spacy.load("en_core_web_sm")` from the constrained 3.15 graph. Use a hash-locked install and load the actual model when retesting. [Presidio metadata](https://pypi.org/pypi/presidio-analyzer/2.2.366/json) · [Upstream reproduction](https://github.com/data-privacy-stack/presidio/issues/2431#issuecomment-6673100519)
- Java uses current Temurin 21 with a matching Gradle runtime. The generated project uses Gradle 8.14.3, Android Gradle Plugin 8.13.0 and Android SDK API 36. A Java 27 migration would require a Gradle 9 migration outside the current Capacitor template. Setup Java 6.3 makes annotations opt-in, so the workflow explicitly keeps the problem matcher. [Latest Temurin 21](https://github.com/adoptium/temurin21-binaries/releases/latest) · [Gradle Java matrix](https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/compatibility.html#java_runtime) · [Capacitor 8 migration](https://capacitorjs.com/docs/updating/8-0) · [Setup Java 6.3 release](https://github.com/actions/setup-java/releases/tag/v6.3.0)
- Upstream consumers own the transitive terminal-formatting major transitions. The reviewed pure-ESM and output changes cover ANSI detection/styling, emoji patterns, string width, and sisteransi. There are no direct imports of these transitive libraries from shipped or CI code. Both npm example packaging and the runtime suite exercise the parent tools. [ansi-regex](https://github.com/chalk/ansi-regex/releases) · [ansi-styles](https://github.com/chalk/ansi-styles/releases) · [emoji-regex](https://github.com/mathiasbynens/emoji-regex/releases) · [string-width](https://github.com/sindresorhus/string-width/releases) · [strip-ansi](https://github.com/chalk/strip-ansi/releases) · [sisteransi](https://www.npmjs.com/package/sisteransi)
- Both Playwright images use the registry digest for the locked Playwright 1.65.1 release. The workflow regression test checks the tag and digest in both jobs against the npm version. BuildKit’s canonical and fallback registry tags resolve to the same manifest digest. Betterleaks 1.10.1 ships the same configuration checksum and 203-rule catalog as the prior patch. [Playwright release notes](https://playwright.dev/docs/release-notes) · [Buildx release](https://github.com/docker/buildx/releases/tag/v0.39.1) · [Betterleaks release](https://github.com/betterleaks/betterleaks/releases/tag/v1.10.1)

## Upstream reports and retained workarounds

| Report | Reproduction and downstream decision |
| --- | --- |
| [Browser Commander #193](https://github.com/link-foundation/browser-commander/issues/193) | `npm ls` shows Command Stream 2.6.0 and Links Notation 0.25.2 under 0.35.0, alongside this project's newer direct dependencies. Keep upstream ranges pending the capture and config migration. |
| [Lino i18n #45](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n/issues/45) | `npm ls` shows the 0.9 and 1.0 codecs installed side by side. Keep the i18n consumer's 0.9 range pending upstream roundtrip tests. |
| [Actions Toolkit #2582](https://github.com/actions/toolkit/issues/2582) | The current SDK expects `archiver.create`; Archiver 8 exports named archive classes and no longer resolves `archiver-utils` or its glob. Keep the targeted glob override until the SDK migrates. |
| [Scrubadub #157](https://github.com/LeapBeyond/scrubadub/issues/157) | Scrubadub 2.0.1 pins TextBlob 0.15.3, whose two invalid escape sequences warn on CPython 3.14. The current TextBlob passed the same offline scanner smoke in an isolated overlay with `-W error::SyntaxWarning`. Keep the upstream-required pin in the real graph. |
| [Existing upstream reports from PR 103](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/main/dev/log/issues/102/pulls/103/upstream/reports.json) | Covers Node setup-cache ordering, Buildx failover, artifact download/ZIP behavior, the local temp cleanup adapter, Pages, Python wheels and workflow lint grammar. The scoped workarounds remain in place. |
| [Lychee #2297](https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee/issues/2297) | Current Lychee retry classification still misses connect/TLS resets. The existing bounded link recheck remains in the workflow. |

Fixes #223

The merged Dependabot updates left main failing Prettier. Apply the locked formatter's output and preserve the merged dependency upgrades. The earlier npm audit failures in #212 came from a picomatch advisory that GitHub has since withdrawn. The later security run on main and the refreshed npm locks pass audit.

- Regenerate all three npm locks, the frozen Deno graph and both Python hash resolutions. Update active workflow, image, scanner and release-tool pins and add Dependabot coverage for the Python resolution named in the issue.
- Move to Command Stream 3 and Lino Objects Codec 1. The codec requires Node.js 26.13.1 or later. The major changeset records the new Node floor. Bun and Deno remain supported.
- Use native \`RegExp.escape\` and update regression tests to verify the Bun pin, Playwright image digest and Python audit coverage.
- Keep the latest compatible Python 3.14 and Temurin 21 releases because the current Presidio and Capacitor toolchains constrain their newer majors. The version inventories give the reason for each retained dependency version.

### Reproduction and verification

Run \`npx --yes prettier@3.10.1 --check docs/COVERAGE.md docs/case-studies/issue-128/research/open-source-pii.md\` at main commit \`5c2804c\` to reproduce both formatting errors. The same command passes after the fix, and the existing CI formatting job covers both files.

Three clean npm installs, three npm audits, the frozen Deno graph, Deno audit, both Python hash audits and a real spaCy model load passed locally. The existing offline benchmark completed all 224 cases, with all 210 expected spans found by the sanitizer. Focused regressions passed on Node, Bun and Deno. The app built locally and both Capacitor native projects generated successfully. The signed mobile jobs require repository configuration and run through the manual workflow. Post-merge CI on the default branch remains to be verified.

The dependency tables, baseline logs, migration sources and benchmark results are recorded with the PR. [Research and verification](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/tree/issue-223-f7aee62ca003/dev/log/issues/223/pulls/224)

- Codec 1 compatibility in [Lino i18n #45](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n/issues/45)
- Archiver 8 migration and glob deprecation in [Actions Toolkit #2582](https://github.com/actions/toolkit/issues/2582)
- TextBlob compatibility and Python syntax warnings in [Scrubadub #157](https://github.com/LeapBeyond/scrubadub/issues/157)
EOF

## Live LLM gateways

Source and documentation review with [pinned revisions and evidence](../case-studies/issue-218/gateway-evidence.md).
Transport rechunking refers to HTTP body bytes. Delta rechunking refers to
token fragments separated by complete, decoded provider events.

| Project and deployment                                                                        | Credential and map ownership                                                                                                 | Reply restoration                                                                                                                                    | Request scan failure                                                                                                                  |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| This project · scanner API and [adapter example](../LIVE-REPLIES.md)                          | The gateway authenticates session ownership, manages upstream credentials and supplies its private map.                      | Bounded UTF-8 cursor for transport splits, plus one text cursor per decoded field or index for JSON/SSE. Credential entries stay masked.             | A required detector error blocks sanitization. The example model adapter offers an explicit deterministic-only fallback.              |
| ai-proxy · reverse proxy plus CONNECT tunneling or opt-in TLS inspection                      | Provider auth headers follow the upstream route; the restorable map belongs to an active request. Blind CONNECT cannot scan. | Bounded rolling HTTP byte buffer for JSON/SSE content. Chat typed deltas are assembled and emitted again; native byte SSE and Responses completion events take separate paths. | Pre-call guardrail errors propagate.                                                                                                  |
| LLM Shield Proxy · standalone gateway and LiteLLM guardrail integration                       | Distinct virtual and upstream keys in standalone mode. Management APIs have no authentication. | SSE text-delta tail buffer per content block; separately assembled tool JSON.                                                                        | A strict scan-failure policy was unverified.                                                                                          |

# Contributing to sensitive-data-sanitizer

## Development Workflow

Use Node.js 26.13.1 with npm 12.2.3 for development and release tooling.
Changesets 3 requires a supported Node.js 22.11, 24, or 26+ runtime.

1. **Fork the repository** and clone your fork
2. **Create a feature branch**: `git checkout -b feature/my-feature`
3. **Install dependencies**: `bun install` (or `npm install`)
4. **Make your changes**
5. **Run local checks**: `bun run check`
6. **Create a changeset**: `bun run changeset`
7. **Commit and push** (pre-commit hooks will run automatically)
8. **Create a Pull Request**

## Code Standards

### File Size Limits

**Maximum 1500 lines per file** (enforced via ESLint `max-lines` rule and CI `check-file-line-limits` job).

This benefits both AI and human developers by ensuring files remain readable and maintainable.

### Formatting and Linting

All code must pass:

```bash
# Check formatting
bun run format:check

# Check linting
bun run lint

# Run all checks
bun run check
```

Python helpers in `scripts/`, `examples/`, and `experiments/` also pass pinned
Ruff lint and formatting checks. Use the Python release in `.python-version`; importing optional
benchmark or example dependencies is not required for these static checks:

```bash
pipx run --spec ruff==0.17.6 ruff check .
pipx run --spec ruff==0.17.6 ruff format --check .
# Apply formatting locally
pipx run --spec ruff==0.17.6 ruff format .
```

Immutable downloaded evidence under `dev/log/` and `docs/case-studies/` is
excluded. CodeQL additionally scans shipped Python helpers and examples.
The preview container smoke check accepts `CI_SCRIPTS_DEBUG=1` to report tool
locations while keeping credentials out of logs.

Security CI also audits every tracked `requirements*.txt` file, including the
benchmark dependencies. It resolves transitive wheel metadata and hashes with
`uv==0.13.9`, then checks that complete resolution with `pip-audit==2.10.1`.
The audit reads metadata without installing NLP packages or executing build
hooks. A separate CI smoke check installs the hash-locked benchmark graph and
model, then exercises the actual offline scanners. New Python manifest formats
require an explicit audit mapping. To reproduce with those
two tools on PATH, run `python3 scripts/audit-python-dependencies.py`.

The pre-commit hook runs automatically, but you can also manually format and fix:

```bash
# Auto-fix formatting
bun run format

# Contributing to sensitive-data-sanitizer

## Development Workflow

Use Node.js 26.13.1 with npm 12.2.3 for development and release tooling.
Changesets 3 requires a supported Node.js 22.11, 24, or 26+ runtime.

1. **Fork the repository** and clone your fork
2. **Create a feature branch**: `git checkout -b feature/my-feature`
3. **Install dependencies**: `bun install` (or `npm install`)
4. **Make your changes**
5. **Run local checks**: `bun run check`
6. **Create a changeset**: `bun run changeset`
7. **Commit and push** (pre-commit hooks will run automatically)
8. **Create a Pull Request**

## Code Standards

### File Size Limits

**Maximum 1500 lines per file** (enforced via ESLint `max-lines` rule and CI `check-file-line-limits` job).

This benefits both AI and human developers by ensuring files remain readable and maintainable.

### Formatting and Linting

All code must pass:

```bash
# Check formatting
bun run format:check

# Check linting
bun run lint

# Run all checks
bun run check
```

Python helpers in `scripts/`, `examples/`, and `experiments/` also pass pinned
Ruff lint and formatting checks. Use the Python release in `.python-version`; importing optional
benchmark or example dependencies is not required for these static checks:

```bash
pipx run --spec ruff==0.17.6 ruff check .
pipx run --spec ruff==0.17.6 ruff format --check .
# Apply formatting locally
pipx run --spec ruff==0.17.6 ruff format .
```

Immutable downloaded evidence under `dev/log/` and `docs/case-studies/` is
excluded. CodeQL additionally scans shipped Python helpers and examples.
The preview container smoke check accepts `CI_SCRIPTS_DEBUG=1` to report tool
locations while keeping credentials out of logs.

Security CI also audits every tracked `requirements*.txt` file, including the
benchmark dependencies. It resolves transitive wheel metadata and hashes with
`uv==0.13.9`, then checks that complete resolution with `pip-audit==2.10.1`.
The audit reads metadata without installing NLP packages or executing build
hooks. A separate CI smoke check installs the hash-locked benchmark graph and
model, then exercises the actual offline scanners. New Python manifest formats
require an explicit audit mapping. To reproduce with those
two tools on PATH, run `python3 scripts/audit-python-dependencies.py`.

name: Rerun unacquired jobs

# When GitHub cannot provide a hosted runner (usually macOS arm64 under
# capacity constraints) it gives up on the job with "The job was not acquired
# by Runner of type hosted even after multiple attempts". No code ran, yet the
# run is red and a push to main releases nothing. A job can also stall in its
# setup (a hung `npm ci` on one host) until a timeout ends it; when that was
# the job's `timeout-minutes`, the job and the whole run end cancelled. This
# reruns such runs, at most twice, and only when no job that ran tests failed.
# A cancelled run is rerun only when a job stalled in its setup, so a run that
# someone cancelled stays cancelled.
on:
  # Runs the default branch's code, reads only numeric run IDs from the event,
  # and never checks out the commit of the run it inspects.
  workflow_run: # zizmor: ignore[dangerous-triggers]
    workflows:
      - Checks and release
      - Example app
      - Security
      - Broken Link Checker
      - Workflows
    types: [completed]

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  GIT_CONFIG_COUNT: '1'
  GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0: init.defaultBranch
  GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0: main

jobs:
  rerun:
    name: Rerun jobs that never got a runner
    # Attempts 1 and 2 may be rerun; the script repeats these checks.
    if: >-
      (github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'failure' ||
      github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'cancelled' ||
      github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'timed_out') &&
      github.event.workflow_run.run_attempt < 3
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 5
    concurrency:
      group: rerun-unacquired-${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    permissions:
      actions: write
      # Reads the timeout annotations of stalled jobs' check runs.
      checks: read
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-node

      - name: Rerun the run when only runner acquisition or setup failed
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: [REDACTED] github.token }}
        run: node scripts/rerun-unacquired.mjs rerun

          path: examples/universal-app/out
          if-no-files-found: error

  android-build:
    name: Build Android app
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && vars.EXAMPLE_APP_ENABLE_ANDROID_BUILD == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 30
    concurrency:
      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-android-build
      cancel-in-progress: true
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-node
        with:
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: examples/universal-app/package-lock.json

      - name: Setup Java
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6.3.0
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '21.0.13+2.1'
          problem-matcher: true

      - name: Setup Android SDK
        uses: android-actions/setup-android@be39fa834029ff78f1a44aa3bb0819b8fc2bd8fd # v4.0.4

      - name: Install app dependencies
        shell: bash
        env:
          BUDGET_ATTEMPTS: '2'
        run: bash scripts/run-with-budget-warning.sh 60 "Example app dependency install" npm ci --prefix examples/universal-app --no-audit --no-fund

      - name: Add Android project
        run: npm --prefix examples/universal-app run mobile:android:add

      - name: Build Android project
        run: npm --prefix examples/universal-app run mobile:android:build

      - name: Upload Android output
        uses: ./.github/actions/artifact-transport
        with:
          name: universal-example-android
          path: |
            examples/universal-app/android/app/build/outputs/**/*.apk
            examples/universal-app/android/app/build/outputs/**/*.aab
          if-no-files-found: error

  ios-build:

    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && vars.EXAMPLE_APP_ENABLE_IOS_BUILD == 'true'
    runs-on: macos-26-intel
    timeout-minutes: 30
    concurrency:
      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-ios-build
      cancel-in-progress: true
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-node
        with:
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: examples/universal-app/package-lock.json

      - name: Install app dependencies
        shell: bash
        env:
          BUDGET_ATTEMPTS: '2'
        run: bash scripts/run-with-budget-warning.sh 60 "Example app dependency install" npm ci --prefix examples/universal-app --no-audit --no-fund

      - name: Add iOS project
        run: npm --prefix examples/universal-app run mobile:ios:add

      - name: Build iOS project
        run: npm --prefix examples/universal-app run mobile:ios:build

  # Exercise the same publishing environment on PRs, where the writer is skipped.
